uncited: Unlike its sibling [Simplex Noise](978-simplex-noise.md) or [Value Noise](4008-value-noise.md), which define the local interpolation behavior, FBM defines the spectral summation strategy across scales [22470-tileable-noise-generation.md].
FBM constructs a fractal noise field by evaluating a base gradient noise function (such as [Perlin Noise](3860-gradient-based-noise-perlin-simplex.md)) at multiple scales and summing the results.
The base noise provides smooth, continuous values, while the summation introduces high-frequency detail.

The method requires no persistent data structures beyond those of the underlying base noise function (e.g., a permutation table and gradient vectors as defined in [Gradient-based Noise (Perlin/Simplex)](3860-gradient-based-noise-perlin-simplex.md)).
- **Octaves ($n$)**: The number of noise layers to sum.
- **Frequency Multiplier**: The factor by which the input coordinate is scaled each octave.
- **Precision**: High octave counts with high lacunarity can lead to floating-point precision issues at large coordinates.
Using modulo arithmetic or tiling techniques can mitigate this [22470-tileable-noise-generation.md].
- **Boundary Conditions**: Standard FBM is not periodic.
For tileable volumes, the base noise must be tileable (e.g., using Fourier-domain techniques or coordinate wrapping) [22470-tileable-noise-generation.md].
- **Time Complexity**: $O(n)$ per query point, where $n$ is the number of octaves.
- **When Not to Use**: When strict periodicity is required without additional tiling techniques [22470-tileable-noise-generation.md].
